Your body's survival mechanisms are much tougher to defy than people assume! 🧠😮

2- **The Bystander Effect** is a psychological phenomenon where individuals are **less likely to offer help to a victim when other people are present**. 🚶‍♀️🚶‍♂️👀🚫 When there are more bystanders, each individual feels less personal responsibility and assumes someone else will intervene. Understanding this is incredibly useful: it explains why emergencies sometimes go unattended in crowds. It encourages us to take personal initiative in such situations, knowing that our action (or inaction) can be critical. Don't assume someone else will act – be the one to step forward! 💡🦸‍♂️

(Sedā-ye khod rā bālā bebar, na sedāyat rā. Īn bārān ast ke gol-hā rā mīrovānd, na tondar.)
(Raise your words, not your voice. It is rain that grows flowers, not thunder.)

It emphasizes the importance of taking that initial, sometimes daunting, first action. No grand endeavor can begin without that crucial first step, no matter how insignificant it may seem. 🌱✨

Celebrate that beginning – you've started your journey! ✅💖

It encourages us to be aware of our own inconsistencies and to strive for congruence between our beliefs and actions, fostering greater self-awareness and integrity! 💡🔄
